about: Text length limits for organic posts, per channel and field. Each row says how the platform counts (the unit) and where the number comes from.

units.codepoints: Unicode code points. An emoji like a thumbs-up is 1, a family emoji built from several people is several.
units.graphemes: What a reader sees as one character. Any emoji, flags and skin tones included, is 1.
units.utf8-bytes: UTF-8 bytes. A Latin letter is 1, most accented letters 2, Chinese, Japanese and Korean 3, an emoji 4.
units.utf16: UTF-16 code units, what JavaScript's String.length returns. An emoji is usually 2.
units.x-weighted: X's own weighting: most Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and Hebrew characters count 1, everything else (including Chinese, Japanese, Korean and every emoji) counts 2, and every link counts 23 whatever its real length.
units.threads: Threads' rule: each character counts 1, except an emoji, which counts as many as its UTF-8 bytes (usually 4).

extended.when: the posting account has X Premium

limits.notes: 280 on an ordinary account. 25,000 was measured on a Premium account (25,000 accepted, 25,001 refused); X's API spec itself puts no maxLength on text.
Emoji count by their UTF-8 bytes, so one emoji uses about 4 of the 500. At most 5 unique links per post (refused with THREADS_API__LINK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED since December 2025).
Instagram's reference: 'Maximum 2200 characters, 30 hashtags, and 20 @ tags.' The feed shows about two lines before 'more', so the point belongs in the first line.
Facebook's widely published Page post limit. Meta does not state it on a current reference page.
The Posts API refuses over-length text with FIELD_LENGTH_TOO_LONG rather than cutting it. 3,000 is the length the LinkedIn composer allows; the API page names the error, not the number.
The feed may show only the first 40 characters.
Descriptions do not show in the home or search feed.

YouTube documents 5,000 bytes. In a live API test in August 2026 a 9,021-byte Japanese description was accepted and stored whole, so enforcement is looser than the docs; under 5,000 bytes is the safe target. Only the first lines show before 'Show more'.
All tags together, commas included. A tag containing a space counts as if wrapped in quotes, so it costs 2 extra.
A video and a photo post have different caps. A caption written for a photo post can be too long once a video is attached.
Two caps at once, from the app.bsky.feed.post lexicon: maxGraphemes 300 and maxLength 3000 (UTF-8 bytes).
Counted after entities (bold, links) are parsed.
Attaching media drops the budget from 4,096 to 1,024.
1,500 is the Business Profile editor's limit. The API reference documents no cap on summary, so a longer post may go through the API; treat 1,500 as the safe target.

kinds.body: The main text of a post: caption, description or body.
kinds.title: A separate title field.
